corrections.text: The article says Linthicum's position that customers own resilience is "the one HN commenters took in the Bahrain thread". InfoQ's account says those commenters divided: some pointed to the shared responsibility model, others blamed vendor marketing. Only some commenters took that position.

The framing of who owns resilience is made explicit in the sources only by columnist David S. Linthicum and by the Hacker News commenters InfoQ summarises. Dr Ahmad does not say who is responsible, and Dasus, Lundsten and Haraldsen discuss sovereignty and independence, not the provider-customer split. The article's October 27 InfoWorld column is cited but not linked: https://www.infoworld.com/article/4240607/digital-sovereignty-as-a-design-requirement.html
